summary.headline: Schneider Electric Infrastructure H1 FY25 sales rose 20.3% to INR 1,193 crore and PAT 32.1% to INR 103 crore, with orders up 17.5% to INR 1,104 crore.
summary.overview: H1 FY25 sales grew 20.3% YoY to INR 1,193 crore, driven by execution against backlog, with Q2 sales up 21% to INR 600 crore. Orders grew 17.5% to INR 1,104 crore in H1 and 16.3% to INR 572 crore in Q2, and closing backlog of INR 1,389 crore was up about 14%. Gross margin widened about 3 points to 39.5% in H1, but other expenses rose 38.8% on CSR, customer support and risk provisions, which held EBITDA growth to 44.2% and PAT growth to 32.1%. Q2 PAT of INR 54.3 crore included a INR 5.8 crore deferred tax reversal tied to the revised long-term capital gains tax rate.

financial_highlights.change: +26.7% YoY; includes INR 5.8 crore deferred tax reversal
+38.8% YoY, incl. higher CSR and specific provisions

segments.name: Power and grid / transactional
segments.commentary: Management called power and grid the 'bread and butter' segment; Q2 sales mix was systems 70%, transaction 19%, services 11%, with 21% of sales from group companies. Strong sales growth in transactional and services was cited as margin-accretive.

segments.name: Order intake mix (Q2)
segments.commentary: Equipment 47%, projects 13%, transaction 23%, services 17% of Q2 order intake. Intergroup orders are not captured as orders; indicated at about INR 125 crore.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were about 14% of total sales.

segments.name: Government exposure
segments.commentary: Government-linked business is about 40% (plus/minus 5%) of the mix, per management.

guidance_outlook: Management did not give numerical guidance; it described the business outlook as positive and said growth is sustainable.
Kolkata factory expected to start production in Q4 FY26 (calendar Q4 2025), with remaining furnace installation done by Q1 FY27; management said it is on track.
H2 is historically stronger than H1 and management expects FY25 to follow a similar shape.
Management could not quantify the impact of the Kolkata factory on the roughly 20% sales growth run rate.
Next call expected in about 90 days.
capex_capacity: Kolkata (Calcutta) factory: commissioning expected around Q1 of the next year, with production starting in the last quarter of the current year; further furnace installation by Q1 next year.
Management said capacities are being ramped up in plants as needs grow; no capex quantum was disclosed.
Vacuum interrupter factory was referenced by an analyst but no timeline was given on the call.
No utilisation figures were disclosed for transformers or switchgear.
demand_pricing: Management cited data centres, AI-driven digitalisation, RDSS (about INR 3 lakh crore scheme; AT&C losses from 15.4% toward about 12%) and renewables (solar, EV, storage) as demand drivers.
Order momentum described as strong across all segments; Q2 orders rose 16.3%.
Gross margin expansion attributed to better product mix, order pricing, volume leverage, raw material productivity and execution.
Project timing: government tenders reach Schneider about 9 to 15 months after financial closure, typically through large contractors.
Management said it is able to be selective on projects given the order pipeline.
Data centre: the company supplies transformers, LV switchboards, busways, UPS, cooling and DMS; per-MW content was not quantified.
Competitive or pricing commentary was limited; no specific competitor commentary given.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new US administration's climate stance change Schneider's prospects, and is there any conflict between the listed entity and unlisted group entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to growing sustainability and BRSR-driven demand in India and said there is no conflict of interest between the group's Indian operational entities. It did not quantify the sustainability spend budget.

qa_highlights.question: Is the RDSS scheme driving the 11 kV ring main orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; RDSS (about INR 3 lakh crore investment) is a mainstay driver, though state-level political factors cause some deferments.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Indian unit's energy business tracking the parent's trend, with industrial automation weak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company's business is substantially similar; it focuses on substation automation and energy management and does not sell discrete automation components, so there was no dip.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Kolkata factory lift the 20% sales growth rate, and is it on schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: The factory is on track for start in the last quarter of this year, with furnace installation by Q1 next year; the impact on the 20% run rate could not be quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of H1 orders between channel partners and direct DISCOM orders?
qa_highlights.answer: By number of assets, about 2:1 in favour of licence partners in H1; no rupee split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 likely to be stronger than H1, and what is the public versus private split of orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Government is about 40% (plus/minus 5%) of business. H2 is historically stronger, as buyers push to receive equipment by March, but Q3 government ordering does not automatically translate into Q4 sales.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data centre TAM per MW, and what is the order pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a per-MW figure, citing configuration variability. Suparna pointed to backlog of INR 1,389 crore, up more than 14%, as the best pipeline indicator.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the strong cash flow and how is export and services performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Better payment terms, on-time collections, inventory and payables management, plus profitability. Exports were about 14% of sales. Services are cyclical; management is focused on EcoCare subscription services to grow services fees.

risks_watch: Other expenses rose 38.8% in H1 on CSR, customer support and risk-cover provisions; whether this normalises affects margin sustainability.
Q2 PAT includes a INR 5.8 crore one-time deferred tax reversal, which flatters the quarter.
Project timing lags of 9 to 15 months and state-level political deferments could affect order conversion.
Kolkata factory timeline (Q4 FY26 start, Q1 FY27 full installation) and its impact on growth are unquantified.
Services revenue share (11% in Q2) is well below services order intake (17%), per an analyst, and management called services 'cyclic'.
Channel partner share of orders is rising (about 2:1 by assets in H1), and the rupee split was not disclosed.
Management could not give data centre TAM per MW or a national sustainability budget.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and growth, with clear emphasis on execution and margin gains. Management was evasive on quantifying the data centre opportunity, sustainability spend, and the channel/direct split, and it deferred several detailed questions to later follow-up.
key_quotes: So our order booking tracking actually gives us the confidence for future sales, etcetera.
So we have leveraged the strong backlog that we had.
Calcutta is going to have a positive impact on us. But how will it impact the run rate of 20%, not in an actual situation to tell you as of now.

adds.what: Kolkata (Calcutta) factory, production start with furnace installation completing by Q1 next year

growth.why: No numerical guidance; management calls outlook positive and growth sustainable, backed by H1 orders up 17.5% to INR 1,104 crore and backlog of INR 1,389 crore, plus Kolkata factory on track for around Q1 next year with no capex or revenue impact quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin widened about 3 points to 39.5% in H1 on mix, pricing and volume leverage, but other expenses rose 38.8% on CSR and provisions and Q2 PAT includes a INR 5.8 crore one-time tax reversal, so sustainability is unclear.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q4 FY26 start; furnace install by Q1 FY27
rows.why: Kolkata factory is under construction with production expected in the last quarter of the calendar year and furnace installation completing by Q1 next year, and management said it is on track.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 sales grew 20.3% to INR 1,193 crore and orders rose 17.5% to INR 1,104 crore, with backlog of INR 1,389 crore up about 14%, and H2 is historically stronger.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said it is ramping capacities in plants as needs grow, but no capex quantum or utilisation figure was disclosed, so a new announcement is not firmly signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numerical guidance and could not quantify the Kolkata factory impact on the roughly 20% growth run rate, so there is no explicit basis for a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Project timing lags of 9 to 15 months and state-level political deferments of RDSS orders could slow order conversion, though no downgrade was signalled.

rows.label: Data centre and RDSS order pipeline
rows.why: Backlog of INR 1,389 crore is up about 14% and data centre and RDSS are cited as drivers, though per-MW content was not quantified.

rows.label: RDSS scheme execution
rows.why: RDSS is about INR 3 lakh crore, but state-level political factors cause some deferments and government tenders take 9 to 15 months to reach Schneider.

rows.label: Cash flow from collections and payables
rows.why: Management credited better payment terms, on-time collections and inventory and payables management for the strong cash flow.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, orders and the Kolkata factory timeline, but evasive on data centre per-MW sizing, sustainability spend and the channel/direct order split; analysts pushed on margin sustainability, services mix and the Kolkata impact on growth.
